what does vector push_back do in c++ | c++ vector push_back | std vector push_back | how do i use push_back on a vector in c++ => In C++, `v.push_back(x)` adds x to the end of the vector, growing it by one.
what does vector emplace_back do in c++ | c++ vector emplace_back | std vector emplace_back | how do i use emplace_back on a vector in c++ => In C++, `v.emplace_back(args)` builds a new element right at the end of the vector from the arguments, which can skip a copy.
what does vector pop_back do in c++ | c++ vector pop_back | std vector pop_back | how do i use pop_back on a vector in c++ => In C++, `v.pop_back()` removes the last element. Calling it on an empty vector is undefined behavior, so check `empty()` first.
what does vector size do in c++ | c++ vector size | std vector size | how do i use size on a vector in c++ => In C++, `v.size()` returns how many elements are in the vector, as an unsigned `size_t`.
what does vector empty do in c++ | c++ vector empty | std vector empty | how do i use empty on a vector in c++ => In C++, `v.empty()` returns true if the vector has no elements. It does not clear the vector; that is `clear()`.
what does vector clear do in c++ | c++ vector clear | std vector clear | how do i use clear on a vector in c++ => In C++, `v.clear()` removes every element, making the size 0.
what does vector front do in c++ | c++ vector front | std vector front | how do i use front on a vector in c++ => In C++, `v.front()` returns the first element. Do not call it on an empty vector.
what does vector back do in c++ | c++ vector back | std vector back | how do i use back on a vector in c++ => In C++, `v.back()` returns the last element. Do not call it on an empty vector.
what does vector insert do in c++ | c++ vector insert | std vector insert | how do i use insert on a vector in c++ => In C++, `v.insert(v.begin() + i, x)` puts x before position i, shifting later elements along.
what does vector erase do in c++ | c++ vector erase | std vector erase | how do i use erase on a vector in c++ => In C++, `v.erase(v.begin() + i)` removes the element at index i and shifts the rest down. It can also erase a range of iterators.
what does vector resize do in c++ | c++ vector resize | std vector resize | how do i use resize on a vector in c++ => In C++, `v.resize(n)` changes the size to n, adding default values or cutting elements off the end.
what does vector reserve do in c++ | c++ vector reserve | std vector reserve | how do i use reserve on a vector in c++ => In C++, `v.reserve(n)` sets aside memory for at least n elements so pushing that many does not reallocate. The size does not change.
what does vector capacity do in c++ | c++ vector capacity | std vector capacity | how do i use capacity on a vector in c++ => In C++, `v.capacity()` returns how many elements fit before the vector must reallocate memory. It is at least `size()`.
what does vector data do in c++ | c++ vector data | std vector data | how do i use data on a vector in c++ => In C++, `v.data()` returns a pointer to the first element of the vector's underlying array.
what does vector begin do in c++ | c++ vector begin | std vector begin | how do i use begin on a vector in c++ => In C++, `v.begin()` returns an iterator to the first element, and `v.end()` one past the last. Algorithms like `std::sort` take these.
what does vector swap do in c++ | c++ vector swap | std vector swap | how do i use swap on a vector in c++ => In C++, `a.swap(b)` swaps the contents of two vectors very quickly, without copying elements.
what does vector shrink_to_fit do in c++ | c++ vector shrink_to_fit | std vector shrink_to_fit | how do i use shrink_to_fit on a vector in c++ => In C++, `v.shrink_to_fit()` asks the vector to give back unused capacity. It is a request the library may ignore.
what does vector assign do in c++ | c++ vector assign | std vector assign | how do i use assign on a vector in c++ => In C++, `v.assign(n, x)` replaces the contents with n copies of x. It can also copy from a pair of iterators.
what does string length do in c++ | c++ string length | std string length | how do i use length on a string in c++ => In C++, `s.length()` and `s.size()` both return the number of characters in a std::string.
what does string substr do in c++ | c++ string substr | std string substr | how do i use substr on a string in c++ => In C++, `s.substr(start, count)` returns a new string of count characters starting at index start. Leave out count to go to the end.
what does string rfind do in c++ | c++ string rfind | std string rfind | how do i use rfind on a string in c++ => In C++, `s.rfind(x)` searches from the end and returns the index of the last match, or `std::string::npos`.
what does string append do in c++ | c++ string append | std string append | how do i use append on a string in c++ => In C++, `s.append("more")` adds text to the end, the same as `s += "more"`.
what does string push_back do in c++ | c++ string push_back | std string push_back | how do i use push_back on a string in c++ => In C++, `s.push_back('!')` adds one character to the end of the string.
what does string replace do in c++ | c++ string replace | std string replace | how do i use replace on a string in c++ => In C++, `s.replace(pos, len, "new")` replaces len characters starting at pos with new text.
what does string insert do in c++ | c++ string insert | std string insert | how do i use insert on a string in c++ => In C++, `s.insert(pos, "text")` puts text in before index pos.
what does string erase do in c++ | c++ string erase | std string erase | how do i use erase on a string in c++ => In C++, `s.erase(pos, len)` removes len characters starting at pos. `s.erase(pos)` removes everything from pos on.
what does string c_str do in c++ | c++ string c_str | std string c_str | how do i use c_str on a string in c++ => In C++, `s.c_str()` gives a C-style `const char*` version of the string, for older functions that need one.
what does string compare do in c++ | c++ string compare | std string compare | how do i use compare on a string in c++ => In C++, `a.compare(b)` returns 0 if equal, a negative number if a comes first and a positive one if b comes first. Usually `==` and `<` are easier.
what does string starts_with do in c++ | c++ string starts_with | std string starts_with | how do i use starts_with on a string in c++ => In C++, `s.starts_with("pre")` (C++20) returns true if the string begins with that text.
what does string ends_with do in c++ | c++ string ends_with | std string ends_with | how do i use ends_with on a string in c++ => In C++, `s.ends_with(".txt")` (C++20) returns true if the string ends with that text.
what does string contains do in c++ | c++ string contains | std string contains | how do i use contains on a string in c++ => In C++, `s.contains("abc")` (C++23) returns true if the text appears anywhere. Before C++23 use `s.find("abc") != std::string::npos`.
what does string npos do in c++ | c++ string npos | std string npos | how do i use npos on a string in c++ => In C++, `std::string::npos` is a special value (the largest size_t) that find functions return to mean not found.
what does string getline do in c++ | c++ string getline | std string getline | how do i use getline on a string in c++ => In C++, `std::getline(std::cin, s)` reads a whole line of input, spaces included, into s.
what does string stoi do in c++ | c++ string stoi | std string stoi | how do i use stoi on a string in c++ => In C++, `std::stoi(s)` turns text like "42" into an int. It throws if the text does not start with a number.
what does string to_string do in c++ | c++ string to_string | std string to_string | how do i use to_string on a string in c++ => In C++, `std::to_string(x)` turns a number into a std::string, like 42 into "42".
what does map insert do in c++ | c++ map insert | std map insert | how do i use insert on a map in c++ => In C++, `m.insert({key, value})` adds a pair only if the key is not already there. `m[key] = value` adds or overwrites.
what does map count do in c++ | c++ map count | std map count | how do i use count on a map in c++ => In C++, `m.count(key)` returns 1 if the key exists and 0 if not, since keys are unique.
what does map contains do in c++ | c++ map contains | std map contains | how do i use contains on a map in c++ => In C++, `m.contains(key)` (C++20) returns true if the key exists.
what does map erase do in c++ | c++ map erase | std map erase | how do i use erase on a map in c++ => In C++, `m.erase(key)` removes that key and its value.
what does map square brackets do in c++ | c++ map square brackets | std map square brackets | how do i use square brackets on a map in c++ => In C++, `m[key]` returns the value for key, and quietly adds the key with a default value if it was missing.
what does map size do in c++ | c++ map size | std map size | how do i use size on a map in c++ => In C++, `m.size()` returns how many key-value pairs the map holds.
what does map emplace do in c++ | c++ map emplace | std map emplace | how do i use emplace on a map in c++ => In C++, `m.emplace(key, value)` builds a new pair in place if the key is not present.
what does map insert_or_assign do in c++ | c++ map insert_or_assign | std map insert_or_assign | how do i use insert_or_assign on a map in c++ => In C++, `m.insert_or_assign(key, value)` (C++17) adds the pair or overwrites the existing value.
what does map lower_bound do in c++ | c++ map lower_bound | std map lower_bound | how do i use lower_bound on a map in c++ => In C++, `m.lower_bound(k)` returns an iterator to the first key that is not less than k, handy for range searches in a sorted map.
what does set insert do in c++ | c++ set insert | std set insert | how do i use insert on a set in c++ => In C++, `s.insert(x)` adds x if it is not already in the set. Duplicates are ignored.
what does set erase do in c++ | c++ set erase | std set erase | how do i use erase on a set in c++ => In C++, `s.erase(x)` removes x from the set.
what does set count do in c++ | c++ set count | std set count | how do i use count on a set in c++ => In C++, `s.count(x)` returns 1 if x is in the set, else 0.
what does unordered_map reserve do in c++ | c++ unordered map reserve | std unordered_map reserve | how do i use reserve on a unordered map in c++ => In C++, `m.reserve(n)` prepares room for n elements so the hash table does not need to rebuild while you add them.
what does unordered_map bucket_count do in c++ | c++ unordered map bucket_count | std unordered_map bucket_count | how do i use bucket_count on a unordered map in c++ => In C++, `m.bucket_count()` returns how many buckets the hash table uses. You rarely need it.
what does deque push_front do in c++ | c++ deque push_front | std deque push_front | how do i use push_front on a deque in c++ => In C++, `d.push_front(x)` adds x to the front of a deque quickly.
what does deque pop_front do in c++ | c++ deque pop_front | std deque pop_front | how do i use pop_front on a deque in c++ => In C++, `d.pop_front()` removes the first element of a deque.
what does list splice do in c++ | c++ list splice | std list splice | how do i use splice on a list in c++ => In C++, `a.splice(pos, b)` moves elements from list b into list a before pos without copying them.
what does list sort do in c++ | c++ list sort | std list sort | how do i use sort on a list in c++ => In C++, `l.sort()` sorts a std::list. You cannot use `std::sort` on a list because it needs random access iterators.
what does list remove do in c++ | c++ list remove | std list remove | how do i use remove on a list in c++ => In C++, `l.remove(x)` removes every element equal to x from a std::list.
what does queue push do in c++ | c++ queue push | std queue push | how do i use push on a queue in c++ => In C++, `q.push(x)` adds x to the back of a std::queue.
what does queue front do in c++ | c++ queue front | std queue front | how do i use front on a queue in c++ => In C++, `q.front()` looks at the element that has waited longest, which `pop()` will remove next.
what does queue pop do in c++ | c++ queue pop | std queue pop | how do i use pop on a queue in c++ => In C++, `q.pop()` removes the front element. It returns nothing, so read `front()` first.
what does stack push do in c++ | c++ stack push | std stack push | how do i use push on a stack in c++ => In C++, `st.push(x)` puts x on top of a std::stack.
what does stack top do in c++ | c++ stack top | std stack top | how do i use top on a stack in c++ => In C++, `st.top()` returns the top element of a std::stack without removing it.
what does stack pop do in c++ | c++ stack pop | std stack pop | how do i use pop on a stack in c++ => In C++, `st.pop()` removes the top element and returns nothing, so read `top()` first.
what does optional has_value do in c++ | c++ optional has_value | std optional has_value | how do i use has_value on a optional in c++ => In C++, `opt.has_value()` returns true if the optional holds a value. `if (opt)` does the same.
what does optional value_or do in c++ | c++ optional value_or | std optional value_or | how do i use value_or on a optional in c++ => In C++, `opt.value_or(d)` returns the stored value, or d if the optional is empty.
what does optional reset do in c++ | c++ optional reset | std optional reset | how do i use reset on a optional in c++ => In C++, `opt.reset()` empties the optional.
what does unique_ptr make_unique do in c++ | c++ unique pointer make_unique | std unique_ptr make_unique | how do i use make_unique on a unique pointer in c++ => In C++, `std::make_unique<T>(args)` creates a T on the heap and returns a unique_ptr that owns it.
what does unique_ptr get do in c++ | c++ unique pointer get | std unique_ptr get | how do i use get on a unique pointer in c++ => In C++, `p.get()` returns the raw pointer without giving up ownership.
what does unique_ptr release do in c++ | c++ unique pointer release | std unique_ptr release | how do i use release on a unique pointer in c++ => In C++, `p.release()` gives up ownership and returns the raw pointer; you must delete it yourself.
what does unique_ptr reset do in c++ | c++ unique pointer reset | std unique_ptr reset | how do i use reset on a unique pointer in c++ => In C++, `p.reset()` deletes the owned object now and makes the pointer empty.
what does shared_ptr make_shared do in c++ | c++ shared pointer make_shared | std shared_ptr make_shared | how do i use make_shared on a shared pointer in c++ => In C++, `std::make_shared<T>(args)` creates a T and a shared_ptr to it in one efficient step.
what does shared_ptr use_count do in c++ | c++ shared pointer use_count | std shared_ptr use_count | how do i use use_count on a shared pointer in c++ => In C++, `p.use_count()` returns how many shared_ptrs share ownership of the object.
what does std sort do in c++ | c++ std::sort | how do i use sort in c++ | sort function c++ => In C++, `std::sort(v.begin(), v.end())` sorts a range from small to big. Pass a comparator like `std::greater<>()` to sort the other way. It is in `<algorithm>`.
what does std stable_sort do in c++ | c++ std::stable_sort | how do i use stable_sort in c++ | stable_sort function c++ => In C++, `std::stable_sort` sorts like sort but keeps equal elements in their original order. It is in `<algorithm>`.
what does std reverse do in c++ | c++ std::reverse | how do i use reverse in c++ | reverse function c++ => In C++, `std::reverse(v.begin(), v.end())` flips the order of a range in place. It is in `<algorithm>`.
what does std find do in c++ | c++ std::find | how do i use find in c++ => In C++, `std::find(first, last, x)` returns an iterator to the first element equal to x, or last if none. It is in `<algorithm>`.
what does std find_if do in c++ | c++ std::find_if | how do i use find_if in c++ | find_if function c++ => In C++, `std::find_if(first, last, pred)` returns the first element for which the function pred returns true. It is in `<algorithm>`.
what does std count do in c++ | c++ std::count | how do i use count in c++ | count function c++ => In C++, `std::count(first, last, x)` returns how many elements equal x. It is in `<algorithm>`.
what does std count_if do in c++ | c++ std::count_if | how do i use count_if in c++ | count_if function c++ => In C++, `std::count_if(first, last, pred)` counts the elements where pred returns true. It is in `<algorithm>`.
what does std min_element do in c++ | c++ std::min_element | how do i use min_element in c++ | min_element function c++ => In C++, `std::min_element(first, last)` returns an iterator to the smallest element. Use `*` to get its value. It is in `<algorithm>`.
what does std max_element do in c++ | c++ std::max_element | how do i use max_element in c++ | max_element function c++ => In C++, `std::max_element(first, last)` returns an iterator to the largest element. It is in `<algorithm>`.
what does std min do in c++ | c++ std::min | how do i use min in c++ | min function c++ => In C++, `std::min(a, b)` returns the smaller of two values. `std::min({a, b, c})` works for a list. It is in `<algorithm>`.
what does std max do in c++ | c++ std::max | how do i use max in c++ | max function c++ => In C++, `std::max(a, b)` returns the larger of two values. It is in `<algorithm>`.

what does std fill do in c++ | c++ std::fill | how do i use fill in c++ | fill function c++ => In C++, `std::fill(first, last, x)` sets every element in the range to x. It is in `<algorithm>`.
what does std copy do in c++ | c++ std::copy | how do i use copy in c++ | copy function c++ => In C++, `std::copy(first, last, dest)` copies a range to where dest points. Make sure the destination has room. It is in `<algorithm>`.
what does std transform do in c++ | c++ std::transform | how do i use transform in c++ | transform function c++ => In C++, `std::transform(first, last, dest, f)` applies f to each element and writes the results to dest. It is in `<algorithm>`.
what does std remove do in c++ | c++ std::remove | how do i use remove in c++ | remove function c++ => In C++, `std::remove` moves the kept elements forward but does not shrink the container, so pair it with erase. In C++20 use `std::erase(v, x)` instead. It is in `<algorithm>`.
what does std unique do in c++ | c++ std::unique | how do i use unique in c++ | unique function c++ => In C++, `std::unique` removes back-to-back duplicates (sort first to remove all duplicates), then erase the leftover tail. It is in `<algorithm>`.
what does std binary_search do in c++ | c++ std::binary_search | how do i use binary_search in c++ | binary_search function c++ => In C++, `std::binary_search(first, last, x)` returns true if x is in a sorted range, in O(log n) time. It is in `<algorithm>`.
what does std lower_bound do in c++ | c++ std::lower_bound | how do i use lower_bound in c++ | lower_bound function c++ => In C++, `std::lower_bound(first, last, x)` returns the first position in a sorted range where x could go, using binary search. It is in `<algorithm>`.
what does std upper_bound do in c++ | c++ std::upper_bound | how do i use upper_bound in c++ | upper_bound function c++ => In C++, `std::upper_bound(first, last, x)` returns the first position in a sorted range with an element greater than x. It is in `<algorithm>`.
what does std all_of do in c++ | c++ std::all_of | how do i use all_of in c++ | all_of function c++ => In C++, `std::all_of(first, last, pred)` returns true if pred is true for every element. It is in `<algorithm>`.
what does std any_of do in c++ | c++ std::any_of | how do i use any_of in c++ | any_of function c++ => In C++, `std::any_of(first, last, pred)` returns true if pred is true for at least one element. It is in `<algorithm>`.
what does std none_of do in c++ | c++ std::none_of | how do i use none_of in c++ | none_of function c++ => In C++, `std::none_of(first, last, pred)` returns true if pred is false for every element. It is in `<algorithm>`.
what does std for_each do in c++ | c++ std::for_each | how do i use for_each in c++ | for_each function c++ => In C++, `std::for_each(first, last, f)` calls f on every element in the range. It is in `<algorithm>`.
what does std shuffle do in c++ | c++ std::shuffle | how do i use shuffle in c++ | shuffle function c++ => In C++, `std::shuffle(first, last, rng)` randomly reorders a range using a generator like `std::mt19937`. It is in `<algorithm>`.
what does std next_permutation do in c++ | c++ std::next_permutation | how do i use next_permutation in c++ | next_permutation function c++ => In C++, `std::next_permutation(first, last)` rearranges a range into the next ordering, returning false after the last. Sort first to visit all orderings. It is in `<algorithm>`.
what does std rotate do in c++ | c++ std::rotate | how do i use rotate in c++ | rotate function c++ => In C++, `std::rotate(first, middle, last)` shifts elements so middle becomes the first one, wrapping the rest around. It is in `<algorithm>`.
what does std equal do in c++ | c++ std::equal | how do i use equal in c++ | equal function c++ => In C++, `std::equal(first1, last1, first2)` checks if two ranges hold the same elements in the same order. It is in `<algorithm>`.
what does std partition do in c++ | c++ std::partition | how do i use partition in c++ | partition function c++ => In C++, `std::partition(first, last, pred)` moves elements where pred is true to the front. It is in `<algorithm>`.

what does std merge do in c++ | c++ std::merge | how do i use merge in c++ | merge function c++ => In C++, `std::merge` combines two sorted ranges into one sorted output. It is in `<algorithm>`.
what does std accumulate do in c++ | c++ std::accumulate | how do i use accumulate in c++ | accumulate function c++ => In C++, `std::accumulate(v.begin(), v.end(), 0)` adds up all the elements, starting from 0. Use 0.0 as the start to sum doubles. It is in `<numeric>`.
what does std iota do in c++ | c++ std::iota | how do i use iota in c++ | iota function c++ => In C++, `std::iota(v.begin(), v.end(), 1)` fills a range with 1, 2, 3 and so on. It is in `<numeric>`.
what does std gcd do in c++ | c++ std::gcd | how do i use gcd in c++ | gcd function c++ => In C++, `std::gcd(a, b)` (C++17) returns the greatest common divisor of two integers. It is in `<numeric>`.
what does std lcm do in c++ | c++ std::lcm | how do i use lcm in c++ | lcm function c++ => In C++, `std::lcm(a, b)` (C++17) returns the least common multiple of two integers. It is in `<numeric>`.
what does std partial_sum do in c++ | c++ std::partial_sum | how do i use partial_sum in c++ | partial_sum function c++ => In C++, `std::partial_sum` writes running totals, so 1 2 3 becomes 1 3 6. It is in `<numeric>`.
what does std reduce do in c++ | c++ std::reduce | how do i use reduce in c++ | reduce function c++ => In C++, `std::reduce` (C++17) sums a range like accumulate but may add in any order, which allows parallel versions. It is in `<numeric>`.
what does std sqrt do in c++ | c++ std::sqrt | how do i use sqrt in c++ | sqrt function c++ => In C++, `std::sqrt(x)` returns the square root of x. It is in `<cmath>`.
what does std pow do in c++ | c++ std::pow | how do i use pow in c++ | pow function c++ => In C++, `std::pow(base, exp)` returns base raised to the power exp, as a double. For squaring, `x * x` is faster. It is in `<cmath>`.
what does std abs do in c++ | c++ std::abs | how do i use abs in c++ | abs function c++ => In C++, `std::abs(x)` returns the absolute value (distance from zero) of x. It is in `<cmath>`.
what does std floor do in c++ | c++ std::floor | how do i use floor in c++ | floor function c++ => In C++, `std::floor(x)` rounds down to the next whole number, so 2.7 becomes 2.0 and -2.3 becomes -3.0. It is in `<cmath>`.
what does std ceil do in c++ | c++ std::ceil | how do i use ceil in c++ | ceil function c++ => In C++, `std::ceil(x)` rounds up, so 2.1 becomes 3.0. It is in `<cmath>`.
what does std round do in c++ | c++ std::round | how do i use round in c++ | round function c++ => In C++, `std::round(x)` rounds to the nearest whole number, with halves rounding away from zero. It is in `<cmath>`.
what does std trunc do in c++ | c++ std::trunc | how do i use trunc in c++ | trunc function c++ => In C++, `std::trunc(x)` chops off the decimal part, rounding toward zero. It is in `<cmath>`.
what does std fmod do in c++ | c++ std::fmod | how do i use fmod in c++ | fmod function c++ => In C++, `std::fmod(a, b)` gives the remainder of a / b for floating point numbers. It is in `<cmath>`.
what does std sin do in c++ | c++ std::sin | how do i use sin in c++ | sin function c++ => In C++, `std::sin(x)` returns the sine of x, where x is in radians. It is in `<cmath>`.
what does std cos do in c++ | c++ std::cos | how do i use cos in c++ | cos function c++ => In C++, `std::cos(x)` returns the cosine of x in radians. It is in `<cmath>`.
what does std atan2 do in c++ | c++ std::atan2 | how do i use atan2 in c++ | atan2 function c++ => In C++, `std::atan2(y, x)` returns the angle in radians from the x axis to the point (x, y), handy for aiming in games. It is in `<cmath>`.
what does std hypot do in c++ | c++ std::hypot | how do i use hypot in c++ | hypot function c++ => In C++, `std::hypot(x, y)` returns the length sqrt(x*x + y*y) without overflow problems. It is in `<cmath>`.
what does std log do in c++ | c++ std::log | how do i use log in c++ | log function c++ => In C++, `std::log(x)` returns the natural logarithm of x. Use `std::log10` for base 10 and `std::log2` for base 2. It is in `<cmath>`.
what does std exp do in c++ | c++ std::exp | how do i use exp in c++ | exp function c++ => In C++, `std::exp(x)` returns e raised to the power x. It is in `<cmath>`.
what does std isnan do in c++ | c++ std::isnan | how do i use isnan in c++ | isnan function c++ => In C++, `std::isnan(x)` returns true if x is NaN (not a number), like the result of 0.0 / 0.0. It is in `<cmath>`.
what does std isdigit do in c++ | c++ std::isdigit | how do i use isdigit in c++ | isdigit function c++ => In C++, `std::isdigit(c)` returns nonzero if c is a digit 0 to 9. It is in `<cctype>`.
what does std isalpha do in c++ | c++ std::isalpha | how do i use isalpha in c++ | isalpha function c++ => In C++, `std::isalpha(c)` returns nonzero if c is a letter. It is in `<cctype>`.
what does std isspace do in c++ | c++ std::isspace | how do i use isspace in c++ | isspace function c++ => In C++, `std::isspace(c)` returns nonzero for whitespace like space, tab and newline. It is in `<cctype>`.
what does std toupper do in c++ | c++ std::toupper | how do i use toupper in c++ | toupper function c++ => In C++, `std::toupper(c)` returns the uppercase version of a letter. Loop over a string to uppercase all of it. It is in `<cctype>`.
what does std tolower do in c++ | c++ std::tolower | how do i use tolower in c++ | tolower function c++ => In C++, `std::tolower(c)` returns the lowercase version of a letter. It is in `<cctype>`.
what does std move do in c++ | c++ std::move | how do i use move in c++ | move function c++ => In C++, `std::move(x)` turns x into something that can be moved from, so its contents can be taken instead of copied. Do not use x's value afterwards except to reassign it. It is in `<utility>`.
what does std make_pair do in c++ | c++ std::make_pair | how do i use make_pair in c++ | make_pair function c++ => In C++, `std::make_pair(a, b)` creates a std::pair. With C++17 you can just write `std::pair{a, b}`. It is in `<utility>`.
what does std exchange do in c++ | c++ std::exchange | how do i use exchange in c++ | exchange function c++ => In C++, `std::exchange(x, newValue)` sets x to newValue and returns the old value. It is in `<utility>`.
what does std setw do in c++ | c++ std::setw | how do i use setw in c++ | setw function c++ => In C++, `std::setw(n)` pads the next printed value to at least n characters wide, for lining up columns. It is in `<iomanip>`.
what does std setfill do in c++ | c++ std::setfill | how do i use setfill in c++ | setfill function c++ => In C++, `std::setfill('0')` sets the padding character used with setw, like for 007. It is in `<iomanip>`.
what does std setprecision do in c++ | c++ std::setprecision | how do i use setprecision in c++ | setprecision function c++ => In C++, `std::setprecision(n)` controls how many digits print for decimals. With `std::fixed`, it is digits after the point. It is in `<iomanip>`.
what does std rand do in c++ | c++ std::rand | how do i use rand in c++ | rand function c++ => In C++, `std::rand()` returns a pseudo-random int from 0 to RAND_MAX. It is old and low quality; prefer `<random>`. It is in `<cstdlib>`.
what does std srand do in c++ | c++ std::srand | how do i use srand in c++ | srand function c++ => In C++, `std::srand(seed)` seeds `rand()`, often with `time(nullptr)`. Modern code uses `<random>` instead. It is in `<cstdlib>`.
what does std exit do in c++ | c++ std::exit | how do i use exit in c++ | exit function c++ => In C++, `std::exit(code)` ends the program right away with that exit code. Returning from main is usually cleaner. It is in `<cstdlib>`.
what is the alignas keyword in c++ | c++ alignas keyword | what does alignas mean in c++ | alignas in c++ explained => In C++, `alignas(16)` asks the compiler to line a variable or type up on a memory boundary of that many bytes, sometimes needed for speed or hardware.
what is the alignof keyword in c++ | c++ alignof keyword | what does alignof mean in c++ | alignof in c++ explained => In C++, `alignof(T)` gives the alignment in bytes that type T needs in memory.
what is the consteval keyword in c++ | c++ consteval keyword | what does consteval mean in c++ | consteval in c++ explained => In C++, `consteval` (C++20) marks a function that must run at compile time; calling it with values only known at run time is an error.
what is the constinit keyword in c++ | c++ constinit keyword | what does constinit mean in c++ | constinit in c++ explained => In C++, `constinit` (C++20) makes sure a static or global variable is set up at compile time, without making it const.
what is the const_cast keyword in c++ | c++ const_cast keyword | what does const_cast mean in c++ | const_cast in c++ explained => In C++, `const_cast<T>(x)` adds or removes const. Changing an object that was really created const is still undefined behavior, so it is rarely needed.
what is the co_await keyword in c++ | c++ co_await keyword | what does co_await mean in c++ | co_await in c++ explained => In C++, `co_await` (C++20) pauses a coroutine until something finishes, then resumes it. Coroutines need a library type to work with.
what is the co_yield keyword in c++ | c++ co_yield keyword | what does co_yield mean in c++ | co_yield in c++ explained => In C++, `co_yield value` (C++20) hands a value out of a coroutine and pauses it, like a generator. C++23 adds `std::generator` for this.
what is the co_return keyword in c++ | c++ co_return keyword | what does co_return mean in c++ | co_return in c++ explained => In C++, `co_return` (C++20) finishes a coroutine, optionally with a result.
what is the decltype keyword in c++ | c++ decltype keyword | what does decltype mean in c++ | decltype in c++ explained => In C++, `decltype(expr)` gives the type of an expression without running it, like `decltype(x) y = 0;` to make y the same type as x.
what is the dynamic_cast keyword in c++ | c++ dynamic_cast keyword | what does dynamic_cast mean in c++ | dynamic_cast in c++ explained => In C++, `dynamic_cast<Derived*>(basePtr)` safely checks if a base class pointer really points to a Derived object, returning nullptr if not. It needs a virtual function in the base.
what is the reinterpret_cast keyword in c++ | c++ reinterpret_cast keyword | what does reinterpret_cast mean in c++ | reinterpret_cast in c++ explained => In C++, `reinterpret_cast` treats the bits of one type as another, like a pointer as an integer. It is dangerous and only for low-level code.
what is the explicit keyword in c++ | c++ explicit keyword | what does explicit mean in c++ | explicit in c++ explained => In C++, `explicit` on a constructor stops C++ from using it for silent automatic conversions, which prevents surprising bugs.
what is the extern keyword in c++ | c++ extern keyword | what does extern mean in c++ | extern in c++ explained => In C++, `extern int score;` declares a global variable that is defined in another .cpp file, so several files can share it.
what is the friend keyword in c++ | c++ friend keyword | what does friend mean in c++ | friend in c++ explained => A `friend` function or class is allowed to use another class's private members.
what is the mutable keyword in c++ | c++ mutable keyword | what does mutable mean in c++ | mutable in c++ explained => In C++, `mutable` lets a member change even inside a const member function, used for things like caches. In a lambda it lets you change captured copies.
what is the noexcept keyword in c++ | c++ noexcept keyword | what does noexcept mean in c++ | noexcept in c++ explained => In C++, `noexcept` promises a function will not throw exceptions. If it does, the program ends. It lets containers move objects faster.
what is the operator keyword in c++ | c++ operator keyword | what does operator mean in c++ | operator in c++ explained => The `operator` keyword defines how symbols like `+`, `==` or `<<` work for your own types, such as `bool operator==(const Point&) const;`.
what is the requires keyword in c++ | c++ requires keyword | what does requires mean in c++ | requires in c++ explained => In C++, `requires` (C++20) adds conditions to a template, like `requires std::integral<T>`, so wrong types give a clear error.
what is the concept keyword in c++ | c++ concept keyword | what does concept mean in c++ | concept in c++ explained => A `concept` (C++20) is a named rule for template types, like `std::integral` or `std::floating_point`, used to limit what a template accepts.
what is the static_assert keyword in c++ | c++ static_assert keyword | what does static_assert mean in c++ | static_assert in c++ explained => In C++, `static_assert(sizeof(int) == 4, "need 32-bit int");` checks a condition while compiling and stops the build with your message if it fails.
what is the thread_local keyword in c++ | c++ thread_local keyword | what does thread_local mean in c++ | thread_local in c++ explained => A `thread_local` variable gets a separate copy for each thread.
what is the typedef keyword in c++ | c++ typedef keyword | what does typedef mean in c++ | typedef in c++ explained => In C++, `typedef unsigned int uint;` makes a new name for a type. Modern C++ prefers `using uint = unsigned int;`.
what is the typeid keyword in c++ | c++ typeid keyword | what does typeid mean in c++ | typeid in c++ explained => In C++, `typeid(x).name()` gives some information about x's type at run time. The name text differs between compilers.
what is the typename keyword in c++ | c++ typename keyword | what does typename mean in c++ | typename in c++ explained => In C++, `typename` declares a type parameter in a template, like `template <typename T>`, and tells the compiler a dependent name is a type.
what is the union keyword in c++ | c++ union keyword | what does union mean in c++ | union in c++ explained => A `union` stores different types in the same memory, but only one at a time. `std::variant` is a safer modern choice.
what is the final keyword in c++ | c++ final keyword | what does final mean in c++ | final in c++ explained => In C++, `final` on a class stops other classes inheriting from it, and on a virtual function stops subclasses overriding it.
what is the default keyword in c++ | c++ default keyword | what does default mean in c++ | default in c++ explained => Besides switch, `= default` asks the compiler to write a special function for you, like `Player() = default;`.
what is the delete keyword in c++ | c++ delete keyword | what does delete mean in c++ | delete in c++ explained => Besides freeing memory, `= delete` forbids a function, like `Player(const Player&) = delete;` to stop copying.
what is the export keyword in c++ | c++ export keyword | what does export mean in c++ | export in c++ explained => In C++20, `export` marks what a module makes visible to code that imports it.
what is the signed keyword in c++ | c++ signed keyword | what does signed mean in c++ | signed in c++ explained => In C++, `signed` types can hold negative numbers. int is signed by default; whether plain char is signed depends on the compiler.
what is the wchar_t keyword in c++ | c++ wchar_t keyword | what does wchar_t mean in c++ | wchar_t in c++ explained => In C++, `wchar_t` is a wide character type for text beyond ASCII. Its size differs between Windows (2 bytes) and Linux or Mac (4 bytes).
what is the char8_t keyword in c++ | c++ char8_t keyword | what does char8_t mean in c++ | char8_t in c++ explained => In C++, `char8_t` (C++20) is the character type for UTF-8 text, used by `u8"..."` string literals.
what is the long long keyword in c++ | c++ long long keyword | what does long long mean in c++ | long long in c++ explained => In C++, `long long` is an integer type of at least 64 bits, holding about plus or minus 9.2 quintillion.
what is the register keyword in c++ | c++ register keyword | what does register mean in c++ | register in c++ explained => In C++, `register` was a hint to keep a variable in a CPU register. It was removed in C++17 and does nothing useful.
